[[Coaches vs. Cancer Classic]] Champions |bowl= [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result= Sweet Sixteen }} {{2009–10 Big East men's basketball standings}} The '''2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team''' represented [[Syracuse University]] in the [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Jim Boeheim]], serving for his 34th year. The team played its home games at the [[Carrier Dome]] in [[Syracuse, New York]]. Key contributors included seniors [[Arinze Onuaku]] and [[Andy Rautins]], juniors [[Rick Jackson]] and [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wesley Johnson]], sophomores [[Antonio Jardine|Scoop Jardine]] and [[Kris Joseph]] and freshmen [[Mookie Jones]], DaShonte Riley, James Southerland and [[Brandon Triche]]. Although widely expected to finish near the middle of the league, the Orange captured its eighth Big East regular season title, and second outright, as well as the No. 1 seed in the [[2010 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]]. The team also achieved its first No. 1 ranking in the national AP Poll since the [[1989–90 Syracuse Orangemen basketball team|1989-90 season]], and its first in the ESPN/USA Today coaches' poll since winning the [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] in [[2002–03 Syracuse Orangemen basketball team|2003]].[https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5g0gx6y2HHT6GIQs4FoWphzkggY3wD9E69SL00 "Syracuse No. 1 for first time in 20 years"]{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}. [[Associated Press]]. Published 03-01-2010. Retrieved 03-02-2010.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4956590 "Syracuse rises to No. 1 in coaches' poll"]. ESPN.com. Published 03-01-2010. Retrieved 03-02-2010. The Orange failed to win the Big East tournament, falling in the quarterfinals to [[2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]], but their regular season efforts earned them a 1 seed in the West Region of the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. They easily won their first and second-round games over 16 seed Vermont and 8 seed [[2009–10 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen where they were upset by 5 seed and AP #11 [[2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] to end the season 30–5. ==Preseason== ===Roster changes=== Syracuse lost its starting backcourt from the previous season as point guard [[Jonny Flynn]] declared for the [[2009 NBA draft]] and was taken with the sixth overall pick by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Also turning pro were shooting guard [[Eric Devendorf]] and small forward [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]]. The Orange also lost one scholarship senior, power forward [[Kristof Ongenaet]] and one transfer, center [[Sean Williams (basketball, born 1988)|Sean Williams]]. Additions to the team include [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] transfer [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wes Johnson]], who sat out the 2008–09 season because of NCAA transfer rules. Also, point guard [[Scoop Jardine]] returns after [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] due to a stress fracture in his shin. Small forward [[Mookie Jones]] also redshirted the previous year because of a hip injury. Syracuse also brought in three new players for 2009-10: power forward DaShonte Riley, small forward James Southerland and guard [[Brandon Triche]]. Southerland was actually a 2008 recruit, but could not play because he was academically ineligible. ({{college|Syracuse}}, 1996) |roster_url=http://suathletics.com/roster.aspx?path=mbasket |accessdate=February 6, 2019 }} ===Preseason outlook=== The departure of Flynn left many college basketball observers pessimistic about the Orange. In the preseason coaches' poll, Syracuse was predicted to finish sixth in the Big East and were unranked{{Cite web|title=2010 NCAA Men's Basketball Rankings - Preseason |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2010/week/1/seasontype/2 |access-date=March 26, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100321031042/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/rankings/_/year/2010/week/1/seasontype/2 |archive-date=March 21, 2010 |url-status=live |df=mdy }} in the preseason [[AP Poll]]. Arinze Onuaku was the only Orange player to make the preseason All-Big East team, receiving an honorable mention.{{Cite web|title=SU Picked Sixth in BIG EAST Preseason Poll |url=http://suathletics.com/news/2009/10/21/MBB_1021095954.aspx?path=mbasket |date=October 21, 2009 |publisher=SUAthletics.com | accessdate= October 24, 2009 }} ==Season== ===Notable games=== * On November 4, Syracuse was stunned by [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[Le Moyne Dolphins|Le Moyne]], 82–79, in its final [[exhibition game]] before opening the regular season. The loss was Syracuse's first exhibition loss in six years.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=4620949 "Johnson, LeMoyne stun Syracuse"]. ESPN.com. Published 11-04-2009. Retrieved 01-18-2010. * On November 20, then-No. 24 Syracuse upset then-No. 4 [[2009–10 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] 87–71 in the finals of the [[Coaches Vs. Cancer Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]]. [[Wesley Johnson (basketball)|Wesley Johnson]] scored 25 points and collected eight rebounds, and Syracuse used a 22–1 run to open the second half.[https://web.archive.org/web/20091123135152/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293240153 "Syracuse opens second half with 22-1 run to topple North Carolina"]. ESPN.com. Published 11-20-2009. Retrieved 01-18-2010. * On December 10, then-No. 7 Syracuse knocked off then-No. 10 [[2009–10 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in a match up of unbeaten teams. [[Rick Jackson]] scored a career-high 19 points and grabbed 11 rebounds, [[Andy Rautins]] had 18 points and Wes Johnson finished with 17 points and 10 rebounds.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130103100639/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293440057|title="Jackson has 21 points, 11 rebounds as Syracuse remains unbeaten"}}. ESPN.com. Published 12-10-2009. Retrieved 01-18-2010. * On January 2, then-No. 5 Syracuse was handed its first loss of the season as it was upset by then-unranked [[2009–10 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] 82–72. Pitt's Ashton Gibbs scored 24 points and Jermaine Dixon added 21. The Orange was led by Wesley Johnson's 19 points.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100106130751/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300030183 "It's cold outside: No. 5 Syracuse goes 1 of 13 on 3-pointers in loss to Pitt"]. ESPN.com. Published 01-02-2010. Retrieved 01-18-2010. * On January 26, Jim Boeheim extended his NCAA Division-I record for most 20-win seasons to 32, when then-No. 4 Syracuse rallied from a 14-0 starting deficit to defeat then-No. 7 [[2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] 73–56. The Orange's Kris Joseph came off the bench to score 15 points, and Wesley Johnson added 14 points and 4 blocks, taking advantage of the Hoyas' 19 turnovers and 20 personal fouls.[https://web.archive.org/web/20100128004815/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300250183 "Boeheim takes over sixth place on career wins list"]. ESPN.com. Published 01-25-2010. Retrieved 01-25-2010. *On February 27, the Orange clinched its eighth Big East regular season title and a No. 1 seed in the Big East tournament by beating No. 8 Villanova, 95–77. The game also set the NCAA on-campus basketball attendance record, with 34,616 spectators present. Three days later they won the title outright, with a win against St. John's, 85–66. ===Other news=== * On March 1, two days after beating Villanova, Syracuse achieved its first No. 1 ranking in the AP Poll since the 1989–90 season, and its first in the ESPN/USA Today coaches' poll since winning the [[2003 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] in [[2002–03 Syracuse Orangemen basketball team|2003]]. ==Schedule== {{CBB schedule start|attend=yes}} |- !colspan=9| Exhibition[http://suathletics.com/schedule.aspx?path=mbasket 2009-10 Men's Basketball Schedule] SUAthletics.com.
